subject: Billing model consolidation: token floors, context accounting, and discount workback
messages:
From: James Carter <j.carter@olivehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Billing model consolidation: token floors, context accounting, and discount workback

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and batching improvements look promising. Procurement asked me to circle back with a couple of clarifying questions about how Redwood will meter our usage so we can finalize the SOW and discount workback. High level: we need the exact rules so we can reconcile estimates in our budget and commit contractually.

A few specific asks:
- How do you define the chargeable unit when a single user session produces multiple requests (conversation history + re-rolls)? Is context length billed per request or aggregated per session?
- Rounding behavior: do you bill per token, per 10-token increment, or some other quantum? How do you handle partial tokens from encoded inputs?
- Is there a per-conversation minimum or monthly minimum floor we should expect in the invoice?
- If we negotiate a committed volume discount, how does Redwood apply that to mixed traffic (short assistant-type queries vs long-document summarization)?

Procurement would like a short worked example (3 scenarios) showing how a typical week of traffic maps to billed units and the resulting invoice under a few discount tiers. If you can attach a simple workbook, that would be ideal.

Can we get this by EOD PST tomorrow? We are trying to close the procurement approval for a July start.

Thanks,
James
James Carter
Head of Platform Engineering
Olive Health
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: James Carter <j.carter@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing model consolidation: token floors, context accounting, and discount workback

James — thanks for the clear list. Putting Aditya (pricing) and Laura (legal/procurement ops) on copy to make sure the workback is aligned with our standard terms. High level answers below, followed by an ask for the quick call and an attached starter workbook (olive_billing_workback_v1.xlsx).

Short answers (tl;dr):
- Unit: We bill on a per-request token basis (input tokens + output tokens) and then apply rounding to the billing quantum. We do not aggregate arbitrarily across non-consecutive requests; aggregation only applies when requests are part of the same open session and you enable session aggregation in the contract.
- Context handling: By default each request is billed for the tokens sent with that request (so an app that re-sends the whole conversation each turn will bill for the whole history each time). We offer an "session aggregation" option that consolidates repeated context into a single stored context bucket so repeated prefixes are not billed repeatedly. This is a contract-level opt-in because it has storage/retention implications.
- Rounding: We round up to the nearest 5-token quantum on the standard hosted plan. For committed-dedicated deals we can reduce that to 1-token granularity for predictable high-volume pipelines. Partial-token behavior depends on tokenizer used; we normalize on BPE counts before rounding.
- Minimums/floors: We set a monthly committed floor at the contract level (e.g., 500k tokens/month commit). Unused committed tokens do not roll over unless explicitly negotiated. On pilot/PO terms we can set a lower short-term minimum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min call to confirm traffic mixes and pick the aggregation option (session aggregation vs request-based).
2) I’ll send a worked example with three scenarios (assistant chat heavy, mixed, long-document summarization heavy) and show billed units under three rounding/quantum settings and two discount tiers.
3) If the model looks good we’ll produce a one-page appendix for the SOW that spells out the aggregation opt-in and rounding quantum.

Attached: olive_billing_workback_v1.xlsx (starter workbook with fields for us to plug your sample traffic).

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Markus — appreciate the quick summary and the workbook. Two clarifications before the call:

1) Session aggregation: if we opt in, will the stored context count against our monthly committed tokens or is it billed separately (storage vs per-token)?
2) Rounding: for short assistant-like interactions (avg input 30 tokens, output 40 tokens) the 5-token quantum looks like it could add ~10% overhead. Can you show the same worked example with both 5-token and 1-token rounding?

We can do the call tomorrow 10:00am PT; procurement prefers to have Laura or Aditya on the line if possible.

Thanks,
James
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: James Carter <j.carter@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing model consolidation: token floors, context accounting, and discount workback

James — great questions. Short direct answers first, then the three worked scenarios (numbers are illustrative; see attached workbook olive_billing_workback_v2.xlsx for the formulas).

Direct answers:
- Session aggregation billing: stored context is not billed as "storage" separately on the standard hosted SKU; instead, when you opt into session aggregation we bill for the deduplicated token delta per session. In other words, only new unique tokens beyond the stored prefix count toward per-request billing. However, for Private/Dedicated deployments we can negotiate a small monthly storage fee if you want indefinite retention beyond the standard 30-day window.
- Rounding: we can show both 5-token (default) and 1-token (committed volume) rounding in the workbook — example below includes both.

Worked scenarios (week-level summaries) — billed tokens shown after rounding:
1) Assistant-heavy (stateless requests, no aggregation):
   - Avg request: 30 input + 40 output = 70 raw tokens/request
   - 10k requests/week => raw tokens = 700k
   - 5-token rounding => billed tokens = 700k rounded up (negligible change here)
   - 1-token rounding => billed tokens = 700k (same)

2) Mixed (50% short assistants, 50% context-enriched follow-ups with session aggregation):
   - Short half: 5k req * 70 tokens = 350k
   - Aggregated half: 5k req * initial stored prefix 300 tokens (first hit) + 50 tokens delta average => effective billed tokens for aggregated side = (first-hit cost amortized) ~ 250k for the week after deduplication
   - Raw total before rounding ~ 600k; 5-token rounding yields +~1% overhead; 1-token rounding yields exactly 600k
3) Long-document summarization heavy (single large input, big output):
   - Avg request: 6k input + 3k output = 9k raw tokens/request
   - 100 requests/week => raw tokens = 900k
   - Rounding negligible relative to size; billed tokens ~900k

Discount application (workback):
- If you commit 2M tokens/month we offer 12% volume discount off standard rates; 5M/month => 20% discount. Discounts are applied post-aggregation on the billed token total. Mixed traffic is combined into one billed-token pool for discount tiering.

Next steps:
- Confirm call 10:00am PT tomorrow and we’ll run live numbers against your sample traffic in the workbook.
- I’ll prepare the SOW appendix language after we lock the aggregation option and rounding quantum.

Attachments: olive_billing_workback_v2.xlsx (includes the 1-token vs 5-token comparison and a template you can fill with real daily volumes).

DocuSign (preview) for proposed SOW appendix: https://www.docusign.com/olivedocs/OLV-SLA-2025

Best,
Markus
